subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage:
"Mummy, Ma'am said I broke Vihaan's compass, but I never touched it."
"Sit down, Ojas. Take a breath. What happened?"
"My face went hot. I shouted, and she said I was being rude."
"Did you see who did?"
"It was on the front bench. I was in the library the whole period, and Ruchi saw me."
"Then tomorrow we will talk to your teacher together, calmly, with those facts."
"Will she believe me?"
"I do not know. But she should give you a fair hearing."
"Okay. I will not shout this time."
Trisha squeezed his hand.

qa.q: Where was Ojas during the period the compass broke?
qa.a: He was in the library the whole period.

qa.q: Why did Ojas's face go hot?
qa.a: He felt the unfairness of being blamed for something he had not done, and it made him shout.

qa.q: What could Ojas do tomorrow to get a fair hearing?
qa.a: He can explain calmly with facts, such as that he was in the library and Ruchi saw him, and let his mother come along.

qa.q: How might the teacher have seen the shouting?
qa.a: The teacher may have seen it as rudeness and taken it as a sign of guilt, so staying calm and giving facts could change her view.

grounding: A child blamed by his teacher for something he did not do tells his mother, and plans to explain calmly with facts and a fair hearing.

subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage: In the school library, Ramesh Sir held up a book with its cover ripped off. 'Lalremsiami, this was issued to you. Explain.' Heat flooded her face. The class turned to stare. She wanted to shout, It wasn't me! Instead she gripped the desk and took a breath. 'Sir, I returned it on Monday. It was fine then. You stamped it, and the register should show the date. After me, it went to someone else.' Ramesh Sir frowned and opened the register. His finger stopped on a line. 'Hmm. It was issued again on Tuesday.' He put the book down. 'I was wrong to blame you. I'm sorry.' At home, Lalremsiami told her mother, still shaky. Her mother said, 'You did it right. If it happens again, I'll come in with you.'

qa.q: On which day did Lalremsiami return the book?
What was Lalremsiami feeling when Ramesh Sir blamed her?
qa.a: Angry and embarrassed, hot with the unfairness of it; she wanted to shout but gripped the desk instead.
She stayed calm, gave facts about the return and the stamp, and asked for a fair check of the register.

qa.q: How did Ramesh Sir react once he checked?
qa.a: He saw his mistake and apologised to her.

grounding: A girl wrongly blamed by a teacher explains calmly with facts, is cleared, and her mother offers support.

subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage:
Monday. The class plant pot lay smashed on the floor, and Mrs D'Souza walked in to find Harsha pointing at Madhuri. 'She was nearest!' Mrs D'Souza sent Madhuri to stand outside. Madhuri's chest burned with unfairness. She had been at the window watching the rain. She cried in the corridor and said nothing. That evening Papa listened to the whole story. 'Let's write down what happened, calmly. Just the facts.' Madhuri wrote it: where she was, who was near the pot, who saw.
Tuesday. Papa came with her before class. Madhuri read her note to Mrs D'Souza, voice wobbling but steady. Mrs D'Souza asked two other children. Then she said, 'I rushed. I'm sorry, Madhuri.' Harsha looked at the floor.

qa.q: Where had Madhuri been when the pot broke?
qa.a: At the window watching the rain.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling in the corridor?
qa.a: Burning with unfairness and hurt, so upset she cried and said nothing.

qa.q: How did Papa help Madhuri get a fair look?
qa.a: He listened, helped her write the facts calmly, and came with her to school so she could read them to the teacher.

qa.q: What might Harsha have felt when the teacher apologised?
qa.a: Guilty and embarrassed, since Harsha looked at the floor.

grounding: Over two days a girl wrongly blamed by a teacher writes down the facts with her father's help and is heard fairly.
